subject: Production throughput collapse — intermittent NAT split / proxy path errors
messages:
From: ops@citrusretail.com
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Cc: eng_oncall@citrusretail.com
Date: 2026-08-27T09:16:00Z
Subject: Production: severe throughput drop / 5xx surge — Redwood inference

Hi Neha,

We started seeing a sharp throughput collapse in our inference traffic around 09:10 UTC — 60% fewer successful requests per minute and a 4x increase in 5xx responses from your endpoints. Latency for successful requests has also spiked from ~90ms->650ms. The impact began during our EU evening peak and is affecting checkout latency across multiple regions.

We've attached the last 200 lines of request logs and a pcap of a few sample connections. From our initial look there are a lot of retransmits and a subset of requests that appear to be re-routed mid-flow (multiple SYNs for the same client IP). Our cloud provider also reported routing churn in eu-west-1 earlier today.

Can you confirm whether anything changed in your egress/peering or proxy stack? We're seeing 502/504 patterns consistent with a short-lived proxy pool exhaustion or NAT split (requests bouncing between two NATs mid-connection). This is causing retries and amplification on our side.

We need an immediate mitigation (region failover or temporary rate shaping) and an ETA on root cause. Our SREs are standing by.

Thanks,
Aman Kumar
Ops Lead, CitrusRetail

Attachments: request_log_tail.txt (text), edge-trace-spans.pcap (pcap)

Thanks Neha / Aman — quick triage notes from the edge team: 

- Observed a sharp rise in TCP retransmits and 502s sourced from our edge proxies servicing CitrusRetail. The error burst correlates with a subset of client IPs that show asymmetric path signatures (SYN completed on one upstream, subsequent packets reset/continue on another).
- Kernel-level conntrack logs show session table churn, likely caused by NAT translation inconsistency between two peering fabric nodes (we're seeing 'no mapping' followed by new mapping for the same 5-tuple).
- DNS resolution for customer hostnames had a TTL of 30s; we saw a re-resolve during the spike which maps to a different egress subnet. That combined with sticky session limits on the proxy can cause mid-flight rebinds.

Immediate actions taken:
- Removed CitrusRetail from the eu-west active peering ring and routed to eu-central as Neha mentioned.
- Increased per-proxy connection table and session timeout thresholds to reduce churn.
- Disabled aggressive short-TTL DNS caching on our edge for this customer ID to avoid rebinds while provider routing stabilizes.

Next steps:
1) Jordan to coordinate with CitrusRetail and their cloud provider to get their BGP/peering ticket.
2) Soojin to export conntrack diffs and edge proxy logs (attached edge-metrics.png).
3) Marissa to prepare an exec brief if we need credit/contract remediation.

I'll continue to watch the dashboards. Early signs: throughput to CitrusRetail is recovering after the failover but remains 10-15% below baseline; we'll re-evaluate after one hour.

-Marissa Cole
Sr. Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
